title: Monitoring deployments, post-deployment checks, release notes, and incident response
objectives: Monitor a metadata deployment with CLI report/resume and Setup Deployment Status until it succeeds, fails, or can no longer be canceled.
Run post-deployment checks that prove metadata and smoke behavior, separate from data-load checks.
Write release notes that name metadata components, toggles, and known gaps—not marketing fluff.
Respond to a production incident by classifying metadata versus data failure and choosing monitor, hotfix deploy, or rollback—not ignore-errors.
diagnostic_question: A production deploy of LAB_ Apex is In Progress for an hour. Users report a Flow. What do you monitor first, what post-check would have caught it, and when is cancel no longer possible?
definition: Monitoring deployments means watching Metadata API/CLI job state until the org is consistent. Post-deployment checks are the smoke tests after success: components present, tests still green, critical Flows behaving, permission sets assigned. Release notes record what metadata shipped, what stayed dark, and how to respond. Incident response is the playbook when users or monitors say the release is wrong. ([project deploy start](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-cli-reference/guide/cli_reference_project_deploy_start.html); [project deploy validate](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-cli-reference/guide/cli_reference_project_deploy_validate.html); [Take a Deep Dive into Metadata API Deployments](https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2025/09/take-a-deep-dive-into-metadata-api-deployments))
why_it_matters: A green CLI exit while the job is still queued is a false done. Interviewers want report/resume, cancel limits, post-checks that are not 'refresh the page,' and incidents split into metadata versus data.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of an air-traffic incident desk. Monitoring is the radar of the deploy job (Pending, In Progress, Succeeded, Failed, plus newer finalizing states). Post-deployment checks are the landing confirmation: gear down, Flow path works, permission set assigned. Release notes are the NOTAM for the next shift. Incident response is the emergency checklist: is it metadata or data, can we still cancel, do we hotfix or roll forward. Dynamite (ignore-errors) is not on the checklist.
deeper_explanation: Deployments are asynchronous. CLI can return a job ID (--async) for project deploy resume and project deploy report. Setup → Deployment Status shows the same family of jobs. Only one deploy processes per org at a time; others queue. ([project deploy start](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-cli-reference/guide/cli_reference_project_deploy_start.html); [Metadata API deployments blog](https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2025/09/take-a-deep-dive-into-metadata-api-deployments))

The Salesforce Developers Blog (Sep 2025) describes deploy as a transaction: queue, component CRUD, Apex tests, then commit. You may cancel until finalizing/commit; after that cancel is not allowed because it would leave inconsistent metadata. Winter '26 / API 65 introduced Finalizing Deploy and Finalizing Failed states—reverify in your org's API version. rollbackOnError (default in many tools) rolls back a failed job; a successful job that is wrong needs hotfix or prior version (DEVOPS-007/009).

Post-deployment checks: retrieve or Setup confirms components; run a smoke Apex test or the critical Flow as the target user; confirm permission set assignment (DEVOPS-008); confirm feature toggles; confirm no unexpected destructive leftovers. Data-load row counts are a different checklist (DEVOPS-001).

Release notes should list metadata types, destructive items, toggle defaults, test level used, validate job ID if any, and incident contacts. Incident response: classify (metadata missing, test-only, data, permission, integration). Do not ignore-errors. Do not 'fix in production Setup' as the unrecorded path if you claim source-driven development.

mental_model.analogy: Air-traffic incident desk: radar = deploy job status, landing checks = post-deployment smokes, NOTAM = release notes, emergency checklist = incident response. Ignore-errors is dynamite, not a checklist item.
useful_mapping: Pending → waiting in the single-org deploy queue
In Progress → components and/or tests running
Succeeded / Failed → terminal for older APIs
Finalizing states (Winter '26) → commit phase; cancel may be too late
release notes → NOTAM for the next shift
incident → metadata vs data vs permission vs integration
where_it_breaks: Airplanes do not have Apex test stages inside the landing.
Finalizing state names are versioned; confirm API 65+ in the target org.
A successful deploy can still be a user incident.
Notes do not replace Git history.

claims.claim: project deploy start can run asynchronously, returning a job ID. Use project deploy resume and project deploy report to watch it. Never --ignore-errors on production.
Validate also returns a job ID you can report/resume; successful validation can quick-deploy within 10 days.

Metadata API deploys queue (one processed per org), then run component operations and tests as a transaction. Cancel is possible until the commit/finalizing phase; Winter '26 added Finalizing Deploy and Finalizing Failed states.

claims.claim: During incidents, version control remains the source of truth; unretrieved production Setup clicks drift from Git.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: I watch the job with report/resume or Deployment Status. I do not declare done at CLI return if it is async. After success I smoke-check metadata, Flow, and assignments. Notes list components and toggles. Incidents split metadata versus data. I never ignore-errors.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I mention the single-org queue so a long Pending is not always a hang. I mention cancel is unsafe/impossible once finalizing/commit starts—Needs verification of the org's API states. I retrieve any emergency Setup fix so Git stays truth. I page the data team if rows are wrong. I keep destructive incidents on the DEVOPS-009 playbook.

interview_questions.question: How do you monitor a Salesforce metadata deploy?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I keep the job ID. I use project deploy report or Setup Deployment Status until a terminal state. Async return is not success. One deploy processes at a time.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I mention tests as a stage inside In Progress. I mention Winter '26 finalizing states with a reverify caveat. I do not watch Data Loader for metadata jobs. I paste errors from the report into the ticket.
interview_questions.example: sf project deploy report --job-id 0Af… every few minutes until Succeeded.

interview_questions.question: What belongs in Salesforce release notes for DevOps?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Metadata components, destructive items, toggle defaults, test level, job ID, known gaps, rollback pointer—not slogans.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I write them for the next on-call. I include assignment steps if we shipped a permission set. I link the Git tag. I note if validate/quick was used. I do not include secrets.
interview_questions.example: LAB_GateService 1.4; toggle false; no deletes; job 0Af…; assign LAB_Boarding_User.
tradeoffs: Ticket vs Confluence vs GitHub release

interview_questions.question: Deploy has been Pending for 45 minutes. What do you do?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check Deployment Status for another In Progress job. Queue is normal. Do not ignore-errors a second deploy. Communicate the wait.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I look at status.salesforce.com if the queue is stuck with no other job. I do not cancel a peer's production deploy. I keep the job ID. I update release notes with the delay.
interview_questions.example: UAT validate still running; production job queued behind it on the same org—wrong org alias.
follow_ups: Can two sandboxes share a queue?
What is enqueued deploy limit from Apex?
weak_answer_warnings: Start a second deploy with ignore-errors

interview_questions.question: Can you cancel during Finalizing Deploy?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I would not count on it. The blog says cancel is blocked in the commit/finalizing phase to avoid inconsistent metadata. I wait and then post-check.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I mark the state names as versioned. If we are still In Progress tests, cancel may still roll back. I do not hammer cancel. If it succeeds after finalizing, I run smokes. If it Finalizing Failed, I read the report—Needs verification of recovery.
interview_questions.example: Job moved from In Progress to Finalizing Deploy; we stop cancel attempts and watch.
tradeoffs: Cancel early vs let tests finish

interview_questions.question: Design post-deployment checks for Apex plus Flow plus a permission set.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Confirm classes in Setup, run a smoke test, run the Flow as the target user, confirm assignment and tab, confirm toggle, record the job ID in notes.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I split metadata presence from behavior from access. I do not use last week's UAT as this payload's check. I include a data check only if we also loaded rows. I time-box smokes so we do not skip them.
interview_questions.example: Checklist: LAB_GateService exists; TestLAB_Gate smoke; Flow interview; user with LAB_Boarding_User sees tab.
tradeoffs: Specified tests vs a dedicated smoke class

interview_questions.question: Metadata incident versus data incident?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Metadata: missing/wrong customization, failed deploy, bad Flow XML. Data: wrong rows or volumes. Monitoring Deployment Status will not fix Account amounts.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: A permission miss sits in the middle: metadata existed, assignment did not. Integration incidents are a fourth bucket. I pick hotfix deploy vs Data Loader vs assign permset. I keep Git truth for metadata hotfixes.
interview_questions.example: Wrong Opportunity amounts → data team; missing LAB_ field on layout → metadata hotfix.
tradeoffs: One war room vs split owners
Automation bugs that look like data
follow_ups: How do you tell Flow-updated data from a load?

interview_questions.question: Succeeded deploy, feature off. Walk it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check toggle, assignment, wrong org, cached UI, then Git vs org retrieve. Do not ignore-errors a retry of the same zip blindly.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I compare the release notes' toggle default. I retrieve the Flow status. I check if a destructive item removed a needed piece. I check package version. I write the finding in notes so the next incident is faster.
interview_questions.example: LAB_UseNewBoarding false as designed; product thought it was on.
weak_answer_warnings: The job succeeded so the feature must be on

interview_questions.question: On-call for a failed Friday production deploy. First ten minutes.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Open the report, classify failed versus still running, stop ignore-errors ideas, tell stakeholders the org should be rolled back if the job failed, then fix in Git.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: If still running, I decide cancel only if not finalizing. If failed, I paste component/test errors. If succeeded-but-bad, I go hotfix/rollback playbooks. I retrieve nothing from panic Setup without committing. I schedule the true fix and notes. I keep data loads paused.
interview_questions.example: Failed on LAB_GateTrigger coverage under specified tests; we switch to a test list that covers the trigger and redeploy after approval.
tradeoffs: Fix-forward tonight vs wait for Monday
Specified tests vs RunLocalTests in crisis
follow_ups: Do we page the data team?
